title: Which Stretch of the Ledger a Recovery Is Measured Over
content:
The recoverable balance on an Employee Meal Account is measured over a stretch of the account's ledger that follows the payroll cycle the account is recovered on and how lately a recovery was last remitted on it. The recovery recency window for this purpose is 45 calendar days.

**Clause.** Where the account is recovered on a weekly or a biweekly cycle and a recovery has been remitted within the recovery recency window, the recoverable balance is the charges accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked less the recoveries remitted in that same month. Where the account is recovered on a semimonthly or a monthly cycle and a recovery has been remitted within the recovery recency window, the recoverable balance is the charges accrued in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked less the recoveries remitted in those same three months. Where neither holds, the recoverable balance is the balance standing, every charge accrued to date less every recovery remitted to date.

## The stretch each cycle takes

| Payroll cycle the account is recovered on | Latest recovery remitted | Charges and recoveries are summed over |
|---|---|---|
| Weekly or biweekly | Within the last 45 calendar days | The calendar month running back from the day the account is worked |
| Semimonthly or monthly | Within the last 45 calendar days | The three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked |
| Weekly or biweekly | More than 45 calendar days ago, or never | The whole ledger to date |
| Semimonthly or monthly | More than 45 calendar days ago, or never | The whole ledger to date |

In every stretch the recoveries are netted against the charges over the very same stretch, and the result is never read as less than nothing.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical figures)

*Input.* An account recovered on a biweekly cycle; the latest recovery remitted 12 calendar days ago; charges accrued in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked $164.00; recoveries remitted in that month $40.00; charges accrued to date $900.00; recoveries remitted to date $700.00.

*Judgement.* A biweekly cycle with a recovery inside 45 calendar days takes the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked.

*Output.* $164.00 less $40.00, or $124.00.

Had the latest recovery been remitted 46 calendar days ago, neither of the first two cases would hold and the recoverable balance would be the balance standing, $900.00 less $700.00, or $200.00.
